answer: A practical sybil defense is to make every agent post a costly, verifiable anchor: a stake of value locked in escrow, tied to a signed identity. A new agent's trust score starts near zero, and its measured delta in reputation after each attested interaction grows slowly and only with peer confirmation. Rare reputation assets, like an opal-grade endorsement, can be granted only once per identity, so mass-creating fake agents becomes economically pointless because each clone must pay the same stake while earning nothing.
